title: Ready for the Work
independence: Read the committed angle, verified findings, claims, the last two state entries, the full asset manifest, Directors Room and master Phase 4.1. No peer pitch was read before writing this treatment. No subagents launched.
logline: One solid word, READY, follows two useful preparation tools to the professional work their outputs make possible.
stance: Appreciative curiosity. The tangible usefulness earns full screen time while the film stays inside the described workflow and makes no measured productivity claim.

cold_open.picture: An enormous machined TypeSlug reading READY lands with a deep clack across the gap between a little output shelf and a much larger desk. Its long shadow falls over a pen. A truck of the camera reveals that READY is a movable object, and the viewer still does not know which job it labels.
cold_open.opening_line: The machine has finished something. What, exactly?
cold_open.scope: A visibly schematic office metaphor, never a claimed KGS interface. No approval mark, face or named-person caricature.

escalation: The giant READY slug becomes ordinary desk size as the camera reveals KGS, its September 11th announcement, Wingman and its named office-work categories.
A sober corporate identity plate connects KGS to Koniag and the Kodiak region. The relationship is corporate ownership, with no cultural props or implied local returns.
Enter the earlier Army workflow explicitly attributed to AWS. A generic vendor-identifier token enters an email subject slot. DORA is named before its mechanism runs.

The camera travels physically along API retrieval channels. SAM.GOV records come to the mechanism rather than invented prose appearing out of it. Prebuilt logic arranges them into a standardized report.

A match cut enters a visibly separate writing bay. Jumpstarter is named. User inputs feed an LLM and an editable FIRST DRAFT grows outward. Retrieval and generative drafting are established before 60 seconds.
Both tools have made something substantial. Their housings move to the back plane so the report and draft occupy the foreground, intact and useful. The READY slug travels with those outputs.

The professional performs two different next actions. DORA's report is reviewed for a determination. Jumpstarter sections are refined and approved. Show inspection and editing without fabricated mistakes or a literal approval stamp.
The final move places READY at the output handoff rather than at a completed procurement. Useful preparation reaches the professional without magically completing the professional's job.

turn.name: Give the Outputs the Whole Screen
turn.picture: The DORA and Jumpstarter housings slide backward into a deep office cutaway. Their outputs stay large in the warm foreground. The report retains its source tabs. The generated section retains FIRST DRAFT. A faceless ordinary professional's hand draws the report closer to inspect it, then a separate editing surface shows a section being refined. The assets are allowed to be useful before any limit is stated.
turn.earned_change: The viewer can credit the accomplished preparation and distinguish it from the professional action that follows. The ending becomes more affirmative because the useful work survives the boundary.
turn.strongest_fair_counterpoint: If a report is assembled and an editable first draft exists, treating everything as unfinished would erase actual completed preparation. The film grants those outputs solidity, scale and uninterrupted attention, then specifies the remaining professional job.
prohibited_shortcuts: No automatic approval or contract-award stamp

button.line: Ready for the work that follows.
button.image: The original READY TypeSlug settles flush at the edge of the output shelf. Beneath it the now-legible desk inscription reads FOR THE WORK THAT FOLLOWS. The report and still-labeled draft are within the professional's reach. The pen lifts into the foreground and the shadow from the opening now has a visible owner.
button.return_to_open: The same material object and pen shadow return with a precise meaning. READY was accurate at the preparation boundary, and never meant the whole procurement was complete.

sight_gags.description: The heavy READY word lands and gives a tiny desk pencil a restrained hop. The huge verbal claim turns out to be a movable physical label.
sight_gags.target: Generic office-object physics, not KGS or a Native subject

sight_gags.description: An API lookup plug makes a neat quarter turn to align its notch, then a procession of record tabs seats with the rhythm of a tiny precision parade. A miniature spring bounces once after everything else has stopped.
sight_gags.target: Satisfying schematic machinery, no failed lookup or invented data

sight_gags.description: The FIRST DRAFT flag unrolls much farther than its compact roller suggested, then neatly curls its blank tail under. The status is unmistakable and never briefly reads FINAL.
A pen cap spins once into its cup as the pen gets to work. The machine has made an output but the smallest office prop supplies the next decisive motion.
sight_gags.target: Ordinary professional tools, with no characterized people or machines

test.scene: Give the Outputs the Whole Screen
test.against_angle: An audience could fairly object that the machine has indeed finished useful work. Demonstrate that at full strength with a gathered report and an editable draft occupying the scene after the machinery recedes.
test.surviving_angle: The completed preparation survives the challenge. Reviewing the report and determining responsibility remain the professional's work. Refining and approving generated sections remain the user's work. The title means something more exact after the test.
test.source_boundary: These actions illustrate the AWS-described workflow. They are not an independent production audit or a demonstration of a specific actual contract.

throughline_object.continuity: Keep the same notched left edge and a small copper side face across every appearance. It is a movable word, not a badge or approval token.

loops.promise: The machine has finished something. What, exactly? The READY label has no final resting place yet.
loops.payoff: The arrived page and the finished professional task are placed on different depth planes. READY seats beside the preparation output, while REVIEW AND DETERMINATION and REFINE AND APPROVE remain at the professional desk.
loops.honesty: The human role is introduced as soon as the workflow reaches it. The final spatial placement supplies the payoff without concealing a source caveat.

loops.promise: The FIRST DRAFT flag appears with a capped pen waiting in the foreground. What action changes the generated section next?
loops.payoff: The pen is uncapped and the professional visibly refines the editable section. FIRST DRAFT stays visible until the narration explicitly names the user's refinement and approval.

padding_test.why_90s_cut_worse: Removing the full-scale outputs would make the film sound as if unfinished professional work cancels actual useful preparation. This is the strongest fair challenge to the thesis.
Removing the DORA professional action would leave a gathered report falsely equivalent to a determination. This adds the next documented verb rather than replaying retrieval.
Removing the Jumpstarter editing action would collapse two different workflows into generic human-in-the-loop reassurance. The pen and editable section pay the second loop.

asset_plan.freshness: No Sheet or FlightCrate hero and no research notebook. The movie follows a movable cast-metal word across a schematic office workflow. Stage depth separates preparation from professional completion. No Character face, StampBot or culturally coded prop.
asset_plan.new_asset_request: None required. Reuse TypeSlug's held and seated state channels; use existing supporting paper and hand assets. Generic API channels and editing surfaces are set geometry, not bespoke hero rigs.
asset_plan.look_suggestion: Deep marine office shadows, copper side faces, warm white output stock and crisp raking light. Avoid yesterday's lilac and citron notebook palette. Keep practical depth and mobile-readable status words.
asset_plan.feasibility_warning: The pen should demonstrate refinement through an explicitly schematic selection and text reflow. Do not animate a fake factual error or an approval stamp. A report's human determination can be named without portraying a specific vendor outcome.

future_vo_draft:
The machine has finished something. What, exactly?

Koniag Government Services says it supports Wingman, a platform for office assistants. Its September eleventh announcement names contracting, logistics and financial management.

KGS belongs to Koniag, the regional Alaska Native corporation associated with Kodiak.

An AWS case study shows earlier Army work behind this approach.

First comes DORA, the Determination of Responsibility Assistant. A professional emails a vendor identifier. DORA retrieves compliance records through APIs, including SAM dot gov. Prebuilt logic assembles a standardized report.

Separate Jumpstarter tools use large language models through Amazon Bedrock. User inputs become initial sections of contracting documents.

A report and a first draft. Those are tangible outputs.

Give them the whole screen for a moment. Records have been gathered. A blank section now contains text someone can work with. That's useful preparation.

Now follow the handoff.

The contracting professional reviews DORA's report and makes the determination. The Jumpstarter user refines the generated sections and approves them.

The page arriving and the professional finishing are different events.

These are the workflows described by AWS. They don't establish an independently measured productivity result for Wingman.

Still, the useful part doesn't disappear at that boundary. It arrives there.

When the machine says ready, ask what it's ready for.

Ready for the work that follows.
copy_notes: The 214-word draft is a treatment timing proof, not a locked narration. TTS can speak September eleventh and SAM dot gov while captions normalize to September 11th and SAM.gov. The two mechanisms finish their introduction by word 100, leaving room before 60 seconds at the target read. No prohibited performance numbers are used. Source attribution and all final claim contracts remain mandatory.
self_critique: Primary-loop risk is that the audience infers the answer as soon as human review appears. Keep the final placement of READY a spatial discovery rather than claiming the professional boundary itself is secret. Act 3 must give the completed preparation a beautiful uninterrupted look before following each documented human action. The wide output-gallery shot and distinct editing action are essential to earn 120 seconds.
